title.narrative: Practicas de restauracion ecologica y agroecologica para la conseracion de la vida silvestre en comunidades locales de Calakmul, Campeche, Mexico

description.narrative: This project will be developed in six indigenous communities adjacent to the Calakmul Biosphere Reserve (Reserve), known as the most important tropical jungle in North America, and core component of the Mesoamerican Biological Corridor, a crucial area for species movement and habitat of critically endangered and endemic flora and fauna. This project aims at improving the landscape connectivity around the Reserve through reinforcement practices on ecological and agro-ecological restoration on the lands of the 30 farmers trained in the first phase of the project (fiscal year 2012). Project activities include: 1) implement 3 training workshops on the sociopolitical aspects of restoration, applied nucleation techniques, and silvopastoral systems; 2) coordinate an exchange of experiences visit to Las Canadas Cooperative Society in Veracruz; 3) establish 4 demonstrative parcels for agro-sylvo-pastoral systems in conventional pastures and four restoration parcels in areas invaded by Pteridium aquilinum. Project products include: a training manual, creation of maps of the area, a monitoring plan, production of a training and documentary video, publication of the project results in the Xpujis web page, and several electronic media outlets.
